rv.q: For now, Isla remains a beautiful theatrical vessel whose shadows are more fully alive than the story they have been summoned to illuminate.
Like Communism, collaboratively devised theater is a noble concept that mostly disappoints in practice (when it doesn’t actively horrify).
All the artistic elements come together in a wonderful, multifaceted production.

cn.t: Critics praise ISLA's inventive puppetry, live Latin jazz, and visual artistry, but find the 75-minute family migration story lacks narrative substance beneath its dazzling technical execution.
